topics.title: Your Role and Daily Responsibilities
topics.rationale: Establishing what you actually did day-to-day, beyond any job description, is the foundation for all other topics.
seed_questions: What was your official job title and how did your actual duties differ?
Walk us through a typical shift – what did you check first?
What part of your role consumed the most time but was never written down?

topics.title: Key Equipment You Owned or Operated
topics.rationale: We have no equipment records for you, so we need you to name the specific assets you know best.
seed_questions: List the three most critical pieces of equipment you were responsible for.
Which machine had the most recurring problems that never got officially fixed?
Are there any legacy machines with no documentation that you kept running?

topics.title: Major Projects and Their Real Status
topics.rationale: Half-finished projects, abandoned improvements, and scope changes live only in your memory.
seed_questions: Which projects did you lead or contribute to that are still not fully closed?
Were there any modifications that were started but never commissioned?
What project outcome surprised everyone, and why?

topics.title: Undocumented Workarounds and Tribal Fixes
topics.rationale: Every plant runs on informal tricks that never make it into SOPs.
seed_questions: What temporary fix became permanent on your equipment?
When something jammed or tripped, what was the 'magic tap' or sequence you used?
Are there any bypasses or jumpers you relied on during emergencies?

topics.title: Procedures You Actually Followed vs. Written Ones
topics.rationale: The difference between the manual and real life often holds critical safety and efficiency insights.
seed_questions: Which official startup/shutdown procedure did everyone shortcut?
What step in a procedure was always skipped because it was impractical?
Did you keep a personal notebook with the real steps? If so, what was in it?

topics.title: Early Warning Signs Only You Could Spot
topics.rationale: Slight changes in sound, vibration, or smell predict failures but never get recorded.
seed_questions: How could you tell a pump was about to fail before the instruments caught it?
Were there any unique odors or noises that meant 'shut it down now'?
What did you listen for during rounds that no sensor measures?

topics.title: Vendors and External Contacts Who Got Things Done
topics.rationale: The right phone number often beats the official support channel.
seed_questions: Which vendor rep or tech did you trust to solve problems no one else could?
Are there any parts that must come from a specific supplier, even if not listed?
Who should your successor call first when OEM support fails?

topics.title: Tuning Values and Setpoints Carried in Your Head
topics.rationale: Optimal control parameters often exist only as mental notes.
seed_questions: Are there any PID loop values or cutoffs you adjusted based on experience?
What production rate or temperature did you run despite what the spec said?
Where did you keep your personal cheat sheet for setpoint changes?

topics.title: Recurring Failure Modes on Specific Equipment
topics.rationale: Chronic issues that never stayed fixed contain deep patterns.
seed_questions: Tell us about a seal, bearing, or gasket that failed repeatedly despite multiple repairs.
What was the root cause you suspected but never proved for a chronic breakdown?
Which equipment did you inherit that was already 'cursed'?

topics.title: Fixes That Backfired or Didn't Last
seed_questions: Can you recall a repair that made the problem worse?
Was there a 'improvement' project that introduced new failures?
What fix had to be redone within weeks, and why?

topics.title: Training Gaps and Unwritten Knowledge Transfer
topics.rationale: How you really trained people explains what the official programs miss.
seed_questions: What did you teach new operators that was never in any manual?
What was the biggest misconception rookies had that you had to correct?
If you only had one hour to train your replacement, what would you show them?

topics.title: Open Risks and Known But Unresolved Issues
topics.rationale: Your successor must know the ticking time bombs.
seed_questions: What safety or reliability risk do you worry about most after you leave?
Which equipment has a deferred repair that can't wait much longer?
Are there any compliance gaps or pending audit findings you were managing informally?

topics.title: Direct Advice for Your Successor
topics.rationale: Condensed wisdom from decades of experience.
seed_questions: What is the one thing you would tell the person taking over your role to never do?
If they get into trouble at 3 AM, what should their first three actions be?
Who in the plant can they trust to give straight answers?

topics.title: Incidents and Near Misses That Weren't Written Up
topics.rationale: Near misses often hold more lessons than formal reports.
seed_questions: Was there an event that almost caused a major accident but was kept quiet?
What is the scariest moment you experienced on-site that never appeared in a log?
How did you prevent a disaster using only your instinct?

transcript.text: Hello, Srinjoy. Thank you for making time for this. You're retiring soon, and I want to make sure the things you know — the things that aren't in any manual or procedure — don't walk out the door with you. So let's start simply: tell me about your role here. What do you actually do day to day, and what equipment or systems do you know better than anyone else?
